From c4336a07eb6b2526dc2b62928b5104b41a7f81f5 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Willem de Bruijn <willemb@google.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 15:01:46 -0400
Subject: [PATCH] net: correctly handle tunneled traffic on IPV6_CSUM GSO
 fallback

NETIF_F_IPV6_CSUM only advertises support for checksum offload of
packets without IPv6 extension headers. Packets with extension
headers must fall back onto software checksumming. Since TSO
depends on checksum offload, those must revert to GSO.

The below commit introduces that fallback. It always checks
network header length. For tunneled packets, the inner header length
must be checked instead. Extend the check accordingly.

A special case is tunneled packets without inner IP protocol. Such as
RFC 6951 SCTP in UDP. Those are not standard IPv6 followed by
transport header either, so also must revert to the software GSO path.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: 864e3396976e ("net: gso: Forbid IPv6 TSO with extensions on devices with only IPV6_CSUM")
Reported-by: Tangxin Xie <xietangxin@yeah.net>
Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/netdev/0414e7e2-9a1c-4d7c-a99d-b9039cf68f40@yeah.net/
Suggested-by: Paolo Abeni <pabeni@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Willem de Bruijn <willemb@google.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260320190148.2409107-1-willemdebruijn.kernel@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Paolo Abeni <pabeni@redhat.com>

diff --git a/net/core/dev.c b/net/core/dev.c
index 14a83f2035b9..fc5557062414 100644
--- a/net/core/dev.c
+++ b/net/core/dev.c
@@ -3769,6 +3769,22 @@ static netdev_features_t dflt_features_check(struct sk_buff *skb,
 	return vlan_features_check(skb, features);
 }
 
+static bool skb_gso_has_extension_hdr(const struct sk_buff *skb)
+{
+	if (!skb->encapsulation)
+		return ((skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_type & SKB_GSO_TCPV6 ||
+			 (skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_type & SKB_GSO_UDP_L4 &&
+			  vlan_get_protocol(skb) == htons(ETH_P_IPV6))) &&
+			skb_transport_header_was_set(skb) &&
+			skb_network_header_len(skb) != sizeof(struct ipv6hdr));
+	else
+		return (!skb_inner_network_header_was_set(skb) ||
+			((skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_type & SKB_GSO_TCPV6 ||
+			  (skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_type & SKB_GSO_UDP_L4 &&
+			   inner_ip_hdr(skb)->version == 6)) &&
+			 skb_inner_network_header_len(skb) != sizeof(struct ipv6hdr)));
+}
+
 static netdev_features_t gso_features_check(const struct sk_buff *skb,
 					    struct net_device *dev,
 					    netdev_features_t features)
@@ -3816,11 +3832,7 @@ static netdev_features_t gso_features_check(const struct sk_buff *skb,
 	 * so neither does TSO that depends on it.
 	 */
 	if (features & NETIF_F_IPV6_CSUM &&
-	    (skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_type & SKB_GSO_TCPV6 ||
-	     (skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_type & SKB_GSO_UDP_L4 &&
-	      vlan_get_protocol(skb) == htons(ETH_P_IPV6))) &&
-	    skb_transport_header_was_set(skb) &&
-	    skb_network_header_len(skb) != sizeof(struct ipv6hdr))
+	    skb_gso_has_extension_hdr(skb))
 		features &= ~(NETIF_F_IPV6_CSUM | NETIF_F_TSO6 | NETIF_F_GSO_UDP_L4);
 
 	return features;
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

The patch fixes a bug where the GSO fallback mechanism for `NETIF_F_IPV6_CSUM` incorrectly handled tunneled (encapsulated) packets. It consists of two changes in `net/core/dev.c`:

1. **New helper function `skb_gso_has_extension_hdr`**  
   - Determines whether a packet has IPv6 extension headers that require software GSO fallback.  
   - For **non-encapsulated** packets: checks if the inner network header length exceeds the standard IPv6 header size (40 bytes), applicable to TCPv6 or UDPv6 GSO types.  
   - For **encapsulated** packets:  
     - Returns `true` (i.e., has extension header) if the inner network header is not set (e.g., RFC 6951 SCTP-over-UDP tunnels).  
     - Otherwise, checks if the inner IP header is IPv6 and its header length differs from the standard IPv6 header size.

2. **Simplification of the condition in `gso_features_check`**  
   - The original inline check for IPv6 extension headers is replaced by a single call to the new `skb_gso_has_extension_hdr(skb)` function.  
   - This ensures both tunneled and non-tunneled packets are correctly evaluated, fixing the oversight where only the outer network header length was considered.

## Relationship Between Modifications

The helper function centralizes the complex extension-header detection logic, which previously only handled non‑encapsulated packets. The call site in `gso_features_check` is updated to invoke this helper, making the fallback decision consistent for all packet types. The fix resolves incorrect hardware offload for tunneled IPv6 traffic with extension headers (e.g., SCTP in UDP or IPv6-in-IPv6 tunnels), where the inner header length must be checked instead of the outer one.

Here is the root cause:
The fallback logic in gso_features_check for IPv6 extension headers used skb_network_header_len(skb) which checks the outer network header length instead of the inner header for tunneled (encapsulated) packets. This caused tunneled IPv6 packets with extension headers (e.g., SCTP over UDP, IPv6-in-IPv6) to be incorrectly allowed to use hardware offload (NETIF_F_IPV6_CSUM and TSO), leading to checksum errors.

+static bool skb_gso_has_extension_hdr(const struct sk_buff *skb)
+{
+	if (!skb->encapsulation)
+		return ((skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_type & SKB_GSO_TCPV6 ||
+			 (skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_type & SKB_GSO_UDP_L4 &&
+			  vlan_get_protocol(skb) == htons(ETH_P_IPV6))) &&
+			skb_transport_header_was_set(skb) &&
+			skb_network_header_len(skb) != sizeof(struct ipv6hdr));
+	else
+		return (!skb_inner_network_header_was_set(skb) ||
+			((skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_type & SKB_GSO_TCPV6 ||
+			  (skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_type & SKB_GSO_UDP_L4 &&
+			   inner_ip_hdr(skb)->version == 6)) &&
+			 skb_inner_network_header_len(skb) != sizeof(struct ipv6hdr)));
+}
+
 static netdev_features_t gso_features_check(const struct sk_buff *skb,
 					    struct net_device *dev,
 					    netdev_features_t features)
 {
 	u16 gso_segs = skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_segs;
 
 	if (gso_segs > READ_ONCE(dev->gso_max_segs))
 		return features & ~NETIF_F_GSO_MASK;
 
 	if (unlikely(skb->len >= netif_get_gso_max_size(dev, skb)))
 		return features & ~NETIF_F_GSO_MASK;
 
 	if (!skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_type) {
 		skb_warn_bad_offload(skb);
 		return features & ~NETIF_F_GSO_MASK;
 	}
 
 	/* Support for GSO partial features requires software
 	 * intervention before we can actually process the packets
 	 * so we need to strip support for any partial features now
 	 * and we can pull them back in after we have partially
 	 * segmented the frame.
 	 */
 	if (!(skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_type & SKB_GSO_PARTIAL))
 		features &= ~dev->gso_partial_features;
 
 	/* Make sure to clear the IPv4 ID mangling feature if the IPv4 header
 	 * has the potential to be fragmented so that TSO does not generate
 	 * segments with the same ID. For encapsulated packets, the ID mangling
 	 * feature is guaranteed not to use the same ID for the outer IPv4
 	 * headers of the generated segments if the headers have the potential
 	 * to be fragmented, so there is no need to clear the IPv4 ID mangling
 	 * feature (see the section about NETIF_F_TSO_MANGLEID in
 	 * segmentation-offloads.rst).
 	 */
 	if (skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_type & SKB_GSO_TCPV4) {
 		struct iphdr *iph = skb->encapsulation ?
 				    inner_ip_hdr(skb) : ip_hdr(skb);
 
 		if (!(iph->frag_off & htons(IP_DF)))
 			features &= ~dev->mangleid_features;
 	}
 
 	/* NETIF_F_IPV6_CSUM does not support IPv6 extension headers,
 	 * so neither does TSO that depends on it.
 	 */
 	if (features & NETIF_F_IPV6_CSUM &&
-	    (skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_type & SKB_GSO_TCPV6 ||
-	     (skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_type & SKB_GSO_UDP_L4 &&

-	    skb_transport_header_was_set(skb) &&
-	    skb_network_header_len(skb) != sizeof(struct ipv6hdr))
+	    skb_gso_has_extension_hdr(skb))
 		features &= ~(NETIF_F_IPV6_CSUM | NETIF_F_TSO6 | NETIF_F_GSO_UDP_L4);
 
 	return features;
 }

static netdev_features_t gso_features_check(const struct sk_buff *skb,
					    struct net_device *dev,
					    netdev_features_t features)
{
	u16 gso_segs = skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_segs;

	if (gso_segs > READ_ONCE(dev->gso_max_segs))
		return features & ~NETIF_F_GSO_MASK;

	if (unlikely(skb->len >= netif_get_gso_max_size(dev, skb)))
		return features & ~NETIF_F_GSO_MASK;

	if (!skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_type) {
		skb_warn_bad_offload(skb);
		return features & ~NETIF_F_GSO_MASK;
	}

	/* Support for GSO partial features requires software
	 * intervention before we can actually process the packets
	 * so we need to strip support for any partial features now
	 * and we can pull them back in after we have partially
	 * segmented the frame.
	 */
	if (!(skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_type & SKB_GSO_PARTIAL))
		features &= ~dev->gso_partial_features;

	/* Make sure to clear the IPv4 ID mangling feature if the IPv4 header
	 * has the potential to be fragmented so that TSO does not generate
	 * segments with the same ID. For encapsulated packets, the ID mangling
	 * feature is guaranteed not to use the same ID for the outer IPv4
	 * headers of the generated segments if the headers have the potential
	 * to be fragmented, so there is no need to clear the IPv4 ID mangling
	 * feature (see the section about NETIF_F_TSO_MANGLEID in
	 * segmentation-offloads.rst).
	 */
	if (skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_type & SKB_GSO_TCPV4) {
		struct iphdr *iph = skb->encapsulation ?
				    inner_ip_hdr(skb) : ip_hdr(skb);

		if (!(iph->frag_off & htons(IP_DF)))
			features &= ~dev->mangleid_features;
	}

	/* NETIF_F_IPV6_CSUM does not support IPv6 extension headers,
	 * so neither does TSO that depends on it.
	 */
	if (features & NETIF_F_IPV6_CSUM &&
	    (skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_type & SKB_GSO_TCPV6 ||
	     (skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_type & SKB_GSO_UDP_L4 &&
	      vlan_get_protocol(skb) == htons(ETH_P_IPV6))) &&
	    skb_transport_header_was_set(skb) &&
	    skb_network_header_len(skb) != sizeof(struct ipv6hdr))
		features &= ~(NETIF_F_IPV6_CSUM | NETIF_F_TSO6 | NETIF_F_GSO_UDP_L4);
